# Java Audiveris 5.11 (JDK 25) beam-spot chain for the example sheets, from
# oracle/java/SpotsProbe.java.
#
# SpotsBuilder.buildSheetSpots is eight transforms deep before a single beam is
# considered, and Audiveris caches only the last. Graded end to end, any one of
# the eight failing looks exactly like the other seven failing, so each is
# pinned here as it comes out. The private stages are driven through reflection
# rather than reimplemented: a probe that reimplements what it grades grades the
# reimplementation.
#
#   sheet <file>#<n> <w> <h> <digest>       -- NO_STAFF, the chain's input
#   scale beam <b> smallBeam <s> used <u> maxStem <m> interline <i>
#   verticalmargin <pixels>                 -- staffVerticalMargin, in pixels
#   header system <s> staff <t> stop <x>    -- Staff.getHeaderStop, or none
#   erase system <s> x <x> stop <x2> firstline <y1> lastline <y2>
#   destemmed <maxStem> <digest>            -- horizontal runs >= maxStem
#   median <digest>                         -- radius 1
#   gaussian <digest>                       -- radius 1
#   getbuffer <digest>                      -- SpotsBuilder.getBuffer, whole
#   closednoerase <digest>                  -- closing without the header erase
#   erased <digest>                         -- after eraseHeaderAreas
#   closed <digest>                         -- the buffer both thresholds read
#   headthreshold <digest>  / headruns <n> <digest>    -- at 170, kept for HEADS
#   beamthreshold <digest>  / spotruns <n> <digest>    -- at 140, for BEAMS
#   spotcount <n>
#   spot <i> <x> <y> <w> <h> <weight>       -- sorted by y, x, w, h
#   dispatch <i> <cx> <cy> <system>...      -- systems containing the centroid
#
# `getbuffer` and `gaussian` agreeing is the probe checking itself: the first is
# Java's own chain, the second is the same three stages driven one at a time.
#
# The header erase is the one rung that reaches outside BEAMS. It needs
# Staff.getHeaderStop, which HEADERS produces, so `closednoerase` is pinned
# beside `closed` -- a port with no HEADERS can be graded on the seven stages
# that do not need one, and can see exactly what the eighth is worth.
#
# Records are grouped by page: every `sheet` record starts a new one, and the
# records after it belong to that page until the next. Eight sheets are pinned
# rather than one, because chula alone does not exercise everything -- it has no
# small beams, and the one page where extendBeams fires is BachInvention5.
#
# Regenerate:
#   unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
#   JAVA_HOME=/path/to/jdk25/Contents/Home ./gradlew --no-daemon -q \
#     -I rust/oracle/java/staff-impacts.init.gradle :app:spotsProbe \
#     -PspotsTargets="data/examples/chula.png:1 data/examples/allegretto.png:1 ..."
